title: Multiomics Study of a Novel Naturally Derived Small Molecule, NSC772864, as a Potential Inhibitor of Proto-Oncogenes Regulating Cell Cycle Progression in Colorectal Cancer.
authors: Mokgautsi, Ntlotlang; Kuo, Yu-Cheng; Chen, Chien-Hsin; Huang, Yan-Jiun; Wu, Alexander T H; Huang, Hsu-Shan
one_liner_zh: 该研究通过多组学与分子对接评估小分子NSC772864对结直肠癌原癌基因的抑制潜力，虽涉及蛋白-配体对接，但核心是药物筛选而非TF-DNA互作建模，方法可迁移性有限。
abstract: Colorectal cancer (CRC) is one of the most prevalent malignant tumors, and it contributes to high numbers of deaths globally. Although advances in understanding CRC molecular mechanisms have shed significant light on its pathogenicity, current treatment options, including combined chemotherapy and molecular-targeted agents, are still limited due to resistance, with almost 25% of patients developing distant metastasis. Therefore, identifying novel biomarkers for early diagnosis is crucial, as they will also influence strategies for new targeted therapies. The proto-oncogene, c-Met, a tyrosine kinase that promotes cell proliferation, motility, and invasion; c-MYC, a transcription factor associated with the modulation of the cell cycle, proliferation, apoptosis; and cyclin D1 (CCND1), an essential regulatory protein in the cell cycle, all play crucial roles in cancer progression. In the present study, we explored computational simulations through bioinformatics analysis and identified the overexpression of c-Met/GSK3beta/MYC/CCND1 oncogenic signatures that were associated with cancer progression, drug resistance, metastasis, and poor clinical outcomes in CRC. We further demonstrated the anticancer activities of our newly synthesized quinoline-derived compound, NSC772864, against panels of the National Cancer Institute's human CRC cell lines. The compound exhibited cytotoxic activities against various CRC cell lines. Using target prediction tools, we found that c-Met/GSK3beta/MYC/CCND1 were target genes for the NSC772864 compound. Subsequently, we performed in silico molecular docking to investigate protein-ligand interactions and discovered that NSC772864 exhibited higher binding affinities with these oncogenes compared to FDA-approved drugs. These findings strongly suggest that NSC772864 is a novel and potential antiCRC agent.
abstract_zh: 结直肠癌（CRC）是最常见的恶性肿瘤之一，在全球范围内导致大量死亡。尽管对CRC分子机制的理解进展已显著揭示其致病性，但当前的治疗选择，包括联合化疗和分子靶向药物，仍因耐药性而受限，近25%的患者发生远处转移。因此，识别用于早期诊断的新型生物标志物至关重要，因为它们也将影响新靶向治疗策略的制定。原癌基因c-Met，一种促进细胞增殖、运动和侵袭的酪氨酸激酶；c-MYC，一种与细胞周期、增殖、凋亡调控相关的转录因子；以及细胞周期蛋白D1（CCND1），细胞周期中的关键调控蛋白，均在癌症进展中发挥重要作用。在本研究中，我们通过生物信息学分析探索计算模拟，并识别出c-Met/GSK3beta/MYC/CCND1致癌特征的过表达，这些特征与CRC中的癌症进展、耐药性、转移及不良临床结局相关。我们进一步证明了新合成的喹啉衍生化合物NSC772864对国立癌症研究所人类CRC细胞系组的抗癌活性。该化合物对多种CRC细胞系表现出细胞毒性活性。利用靶点预测工具，我们发现c-Met/GSK3beta/MYC/CCND1是NSC772864化合物的靶基因。随后，我们进行了计算机分子对接以研究蛋白质-配体相互作用，并发现与FDA批准的药物相比，NSC772864与这些致癌基因表现出更高的结合亲和力。这些发现强烈表明NSC772864是一种新型且具有潜力的抗CRC药物。
